idiom_name: fieldless enum (+ exhaustive match, TryFrom at the boundary)
implementation_notes: Rust enums are the pattern natively: variants are namespaced, a value of the enum type is never an arbitrary integer, and there is no implicit conversion in either direction. match on an enum must be exhaustive, so a new variant breaks every decision site at compile time; conversion from a primitive is explicit (a cast for the lossless direction, a TryFrom impl or the num_enum crate for the fallible direction). Use #[repr(u8)] when the numeric layout is part of an FFI or wire contract and #[non_exhaustive] only when downstream crates must keep a wildcard arm.
pitfalls: `as` casts silently truncate, and enum-to-integer casts make the discriminant part of your API - prefer TryFrom/num_enum for the reverse direction.
#[non_exhaustive] forces downstream matches to keep a wildcard arm, which silently swallows future variants instead of surfacing them as compile errors.
Adding a variant to a repr-carrying enum changes the set of valid discriminant values; validate against the current variant list when reading persisted numbers.
